answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region, which matches the March latency incident where failover shifted traffic cleanly and restored service in minutes (memory_b2). That is the only playbook that both explains the geographic confinement and keeps customer writes flowing. Rollback (memory_b1) remains a live alternate cause because a release shipped ~30 minutes before the climb, but that memory was an error spike, not region-local latency, so it is the weaker fit. Adding capacity (memory_b3) previously worked only as headroom provisioned before a peak, not as a mid-saturation write-path fix, and circuit breaking or shifting report reads would shed or ignore writes. Failover during daily settlement peak can still overload the secondary or disturb settlement integrity, so that downstream risk is flagged. Cause is not proven; verifying the March record before commit, then failing the region over rather than running a token test, is the single intervention most likely to restore sustained availability.
